text:
Emily Stone: Jan meter reconciliation (Sample A) is in. Summary: 47 accts sampled, 43 within tolerance, 4 outside. Biggest delta is Acct: "Northstar Labs" (hosted) invoice agg +6.4% vs raw telemetry agg. Need guidance on variance thresholds + whether we hold their invoice.

Laura Bennett: thx Emily. What are we using as the acceptance threshold for Jan close? I remember we discussed 0.5% but not sure if we landed it.

Rishi Malhotra: +1. Also: what’s the $$ exposure on Northstar if we hold vs ship? Any other outliers material?

Emily Stone: For Jan we penciled: pass if abs(delta) <= 1.0% at acct+meter_type (tokens/embeddings/etc) OR <= $250, whichever is higher. Northstar is +6.4% on output_tokens only (everything else fine). Dollar-wise: est +$3.8k vs what they'd expect from console.

Talia Benson: pulling from the sheet here (tab "Jan sample A"): Northstar delta is concentrated 1/21-1/23 and only in /v1/chat/completions. Logan/Nadia do we know what could cause +output_tokens on that endpoint?

Logan Wright: Looking. Quick hypotheses: retries double-counted in downstream agg, or partial streaming accounted differently between raw vs billing-ready. Do we have request_outcome in Jan data? (I think not yet.)

Nadia Rahman: We don’t have request_outcome dimension in prod for Jan (ENG-4823 is planned). But I can check logs for unusually high retry rates + compare request_id uniqueness between raw events and billing_agg.

Allison Grant: Also check if there was any backfill job around those dates. Backfills can cause duplicate aggregates if suppression isn’t working (we saw that once in staging). I can look at pipeline run history.

Emily Stone: For context: Finance needs a go/no-go by tomorrow 11am PT for invoice generation. For everyone else, deltas are small (largest after Northstar is +1.8% but only $190).

Laura Bennett: My preference: don’t hold the entire invoice cycle unless we’re confident it’s systemic. But we also don’t want to knowingly send something we can’t defend. Can we isolate if this is a true overbill vs a telemetry undercount?

Logan Wright: I pulled 20 random request_ids from the high-delta window. Seeing multiple completion events with same request_id + different sequence numbers. That’s expected for streaming, but billing_agg is summing all emitted tokens even after client disconnect in a few cases (I see last chunk missing "client_ack"). Might be counting tokens generated after disconnect.

Nadia Rahman: +1 to Logan. I checked raw events: some have `stream_end_reason=client_disconnect`. In billing-ready agg, those are not being truncated.

Rishi Malhotra: If that’s real, that’s not just Northstar, right? Any other customers heavy on streaming that would be impacted?

Logan Wright: It *could* be broader but sample A only has a few heavy streaming accounts. Northstar is an outlier because they have high stream usage + spotty client connections (looks like).

Allison Grant: Confirming: there was a deploy on 1/20 to the streaming collector. No backfill in that window. So likely logic bug not duplication.

Emily Stone: If we ship invoice as-is, support will get a ticket. Console for them currently shows lower usage (console uses raw telemetry agg), so it will look like a mismatch.

Laura Bennett: Options:
1) Hold Northstar invoice only (can we do that?)
2) Ship invoice but proactively flag + offer credit pending fix
3) Ship and wait for dispute

Emily Stone: We *can* hold a single account invoice (manual exclusion) but it complicates close. We’d have to true-up next cycle.

Talia Benson: If we hold, we need a documented reason + remediation plan. Also: do we know if the delta is within an “acceptable streaming accounting policy” or is it plainly wrong vs our meter definition?

Logan Wright: From an engineering standpoint, counting tokens after client disconnect is wrong. We should bill only tokens actually streamed to client (or at least up to disconnect). Right now we’re counting generation that happened after the socket dropped.

Nadia Rahman: I can quantify how many tokens are “post-disconnect” for Northstar in Jan. Rough estimate from quick query: ~3.5k tokens (~$3-4k).

Rishi Malhotra: That matches Emily’s delta number. So it’s basically all explained by disconnect accounting.

Laura Bennett: ok. Then we should not invoice those tokens.

Emily Stone: Proposed: hold Northstar invoice, ship all other invoices. Meanwhile eng ships a fix + we backfill Jan for Northstar (and any other impacted accts) before invoicing them.

Laura Bennett: Approved. Please capture in close notes + add to the Jan controls evidence. Also I want an estimate of total exposure (if other customers impacted) by EOW.

Allison Grant: I’ll add a temporary anomaly alert for high `client_disconnect` rates + large delta between raw vs billing_agg so we catch this earlier next cycle.

Logan Wright: We’ll open a ticket for the fix + backfill. ETA: patch in 48h, backfill by early next week if no surprises.

Emily Stone: Cool. Action items:
- Emily: exclude Northstar from Jan invoice run + document exception in close checklist
- Logan/Nadia: write up root cause + fix plan + estimate impacted accts
- Allison: add interim alert + dashboard link for Finance

Laura Bennett: :thumbsup: keep me posted. And please include a short customer-safe explanation we can hand to Support in case they ask why invoice is delayed.

Talia Benson: I’ll draft a 3-4 sentence internal blurb + run by Emily/Laura before sending to CS.

Emily Stone: Thanks all. (reaction :eyes: from Emily Stone)
